# three-painterly

> Two three.js modules, plain ES modules with no build step. PainterlyPass repaints any three.js scene in brush strokes (impressionist oil, or pointillist dabs). BakedDebris makes explosion debris that you can scrub and rewind: collisions are baked once on the CPU, and the GPU computes any moment directly from time. Both need three.js r160 or later and WebGL 2. Tested with three.js r160 and r187. License: MIT.

Repository: https://github.com/minchenlee/three-painterly
Install: `npm i painterly-pass baked-debris three`

## Docs

- [PainterlyPass README](https://github.com/minchenlee/three-painterly/blob/main/packages/painterly-pass/README.md): options, how it works, limitations
- [BakedDebris README](https://github.com/minchenlee/three-painterly/blob/main/packages/baked-debris/README.md): options, pieces and bursts, brush strokes, displace hook, limitations
- [CHANGELOG](https://github.com/minchenlee/three-painterly/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md)

## Examples

- [packages/painterly-pass/examples/basic.html](https://github.com/minchenlee/three-painterly/blob/main/packages/painterly-pass/examples/basic.html): smallest PainterlyPass setup; B switches brushes
- [packages/baked-debris/examples/explode.html](https://github.com/minchenlee/three-painterly/blob/main/packages/baked-debris/examples/explode.html): voxel towers, three bursts, a wall, a swirl made with the displace hook; B switches brushes, strokes included
- [examples/voxel-paris/index.html](https://github.com/minchenlee/three-painterly/blob/main/examples/voxel-paris/index.html): both modules on a large voxel scene, time slider, brush-stroke fire
- [examples/split-time/index.html](https://github.com/minchenlee/three-painterly/blob/main/examples/split-time/index.html): two bakes, one played backwards
- [examples/paint-pulse/index.html](https://github.com/minchenlee/three-painterly/blob/main/examples/paint-pulse/index.html): music drives `setTime`; WebAudio
- [examples/lightspeed-ram/index.html](https://github.com/minchenlee/three-painterly/blob/main/examples/lightspeed-ram/index.html): no gravity, per-piece `velocity` and `launchTime` along a line, displace hook splits a ship in two
- [examples/grande-jatte/index.html](https://github.com/minchenlee/three-painterly/blob/main/examples/grande-jatte/index.html): a picture that assembles in sheets from one side: pieces on a clock that runs backwards (`setTime(T - t)`, a positive `lookAhead`), carried by a displace hook; dabs vanish on landing and the fine voxel mesh under them appears (a discard in the material and in `customDepthMaterial`); `minStrokeWorld` for dots that grow close up
- [examples/balloon-house/index.html](https://github.com/minchenlee/three-painterly/blob/main/examples/balloon-house/index.html): pointillist brush on a voxel street; a house that flies as a PainterlyPass anchor; debris that rests on it rides along through a displace hook; balloons from per-piece `velocity` and `launchTime` with `timeWarp` as drag

## PainterlyPass

```js
import { EffectComposer } from 'three/addons/postprocessing/EffectComposer.js';
import { PainterlyPass } from 'painterly-pass';

const composer = new EffectComposer(renderer);
const painter = new PainterlyPass(scene, camera, { strokeSize: 7 });
composer.addPass(painter);          // replaces RenderPass
// in the loop: composer.render();
```

Without a composer: `painter.setSize(w * dpr, h * dpr); painter.render(renderer);` draws to the screen.

Toggle with a key (P), to compare with the plain render:

```js
renderer.toneMapping = THREE.ACESFilmicToneMapping;   // plain path only; PainterlyPass tone-maps by itself
let painted = true;
addEventListener('keydown', (e) => { if (e.code === 'KeyP') painted = !painted; });
function frame() { painted ? composer.render() : renderer.render(scene, camera); }
```

Without ACES on the renderer the plain render looks darker and flatter, so the comparison is unfair. With BakedDebris strokes, also call `boom.removeStrokes()` when turning the painting off and `painter.overlayScene.add(boom.createStrokes({ painter }))` when turning it on.

Options change how the scene is painted, not its light. For an overall mood such as dusk (orange light, darker sky), change the scene's lights, sky and fog; then tune `warmth`, `exposure`, `shadowTint` for the paint.

Options (all are plain properties; change them at any time, e.g. `painter.strokeSize = 9`):

| Option | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| strokeSize | 7 | Stroke cell size in CSS pixels. |
| amount | 1 | 0 = original image, 1 = fully painted. |
| resolutionScale | 0.7 | Scene and painting are made at this fraction of the output size. |
| toneMapping | true | ACES fit on the HDR scene before painting. |
| exposure | 1 | |
| saturation | 1.15 | 1.3 suits pale scenes. |
| shadowTint | [0.78, 0.80, 1.25] | Multiplier for dark tones (cool, violet shadows). |
| shadowAmount | 0.55 | |
| warmth | 0.6 | How much highlights lean warm. |
| colorJitter | 0.07 | Unmixed colour per stroke. |
| strokeLength | 1 | Above 1 the shader searches a larger neighbourhood and costs more. |
| strokeWidth | 1 | |
| contrast | 1.1 | |
| canvas | 0.035 | Canvas weave strength. |
| sky | true | Paint the background too. |
| brush | null | The kind of mark. null = `impressionist()`. |
| anchors | [] | Moving objects that carry their strokes: `[{ object, min, max }]`, at most 4. |
| minStrokeWorld | 0 | Strokes are at least this big in world units; close up they grow on screen. 0 = off. |

Moving objects: strokes are fixed to the world, so an object that moves slides under its strokes. Fix: `painter.anchors = [{ object: house, min: [-4, 0, -5], max: [4, 11, 7] }]`. `min`/`max` are a box in the object's own space; keep it tight. `object.matrixWorld` is read every frame. Debris strokes from BakedDebris do not need this.

Brushes: `import { PainterlyPass, impressionist, pointillist } from 'painterly-pass'`.
- `impressionist()`: oil strokes, the default. The table above describes it.
- `pointillist({ purity = 0.8, hueSpread = 0.07, pigments = 12, trail = 2 })`: round dabs of pure pigment hues mixed only with white. Live values: `brush.uniforms.uPurity.value` (also `uHueSpread`, `uPigments`, `uTrail`). `trail`: a fast BakedDebris piece draws up to three dabs in a row; 0 = always one. It reads strokeSize (dab spacing), strokeWidth (dab size), saturation, shadowTint (hue of the shadow dabs), shadowAmount, warmth, colorJitter, contrast, canvas. It ignores strokeLength.
- Set at creation (`{ brush: pointillist() }`) or later (`painter.brush = …`; `null` restores the default). Each change compiles one shader: keep one brush object per brush and reuse it.
- BakedDebris strokes follow the brush: `boom.createStrokes({ painter })` draws oil strokes with `impressionist()` and round dabs with `pointillist()`, and changes with `painter.brush`.

Unknown option names are warned about and ignored.

Extra fields:
- `painter.overlayScene`: a `Scene` drawn on top of the painting with the scene depth. Put BakedDebris strokes or your own effects here.
- `painter.sceneTarget`: the HDR scene colour and depth at paint resolution, readable by other effects.

## BakedDebris

```js
import { BakedDebris, meshToPieces, voxelCollider, boxCollider, anyCollider } from 'baked-debris';

const boom = new BakedDebris({
  pieces: [{ position: [x, y, z], color: 0xd9c4a0, size: 0.25 }],   // one entry per cube
  bursts: [{ position: [0, 1, 0], radius: 1.6, time: 0.5, direction: [0, 0.3, 1], strength: 1 }],
  solid: voxelCollider((i, j, k) => grid[i + nx * (j + ny * k)] === 1, 0.25),   // optional
  ground: 0,
});
scene.add(boom.mesh);
boom.setTime(seconds);   // any value, forwards or backwards
```

Pieces from a mesh: `meshToPieces(mesh, { size = 0.25, fill = 'volume' | 'surface', color })` returns one piece (`{ position, size, color }`) per grid cell whose centre is inside a closed mesh, in world space (mesh.matrixWorld). `'surface'` keeps a hollow shell one cell thick. Colour: `color(x, y, z)` if given, else material colour times interpolated vertex colours. Cells sit on a world grid (cell i spans [i * size, (i + 1) * size)), so they match `voxelCollider(get, size)`. Deterministic; about 3–15 ms for 6k pieces from a 10k-triangle mesh. Remove the mesh from the scene; the pieces replace it.

Rules:
- A piece is launched by the nearest burst whose `radius` reaches it. Pieces no burst reaches stay in place.
- `voxelCollider(get, cell = 1, origin = [0, 0, 0])`: `origin` is the world position of the minimum corner of cell (0, 0, 0); `i = floor((x - origin[0]) / cell)`.
- `solid(x, y, z)` returns true inside anything the debris should hit. It is called millions of times per bake: use a typed-array lookup, not a Set of strings. Remove the flying pieces from what `solid` reports.
- Bake time: about 0.2–2 s for 10k–200k pieces, on the main thread.

Methods:
- `setTime(t)`, `setTimeWarp({ burst, hover } | null)`, `setSizeScale(s)`: no rebake.
- `setBurstOffsets([dt0, dt1, …])`: move bursts in time without a rebake (first 32 bursts).
- `rebake(changes)`: needed after any physics change (speed, restitution, friction, solid, pieces, bursts, seed, …).
- `createStrokes({ painter, brush, strokeScale = 1.25, maxWidth = 34, jitter = 0.16, lookAhead = -0.03, keep = 1 })`: returns a mesh; add it to `painter.overlayScene`. Flying pieces become brush strokes. The look comes from `brush` (default: `painter.brush`, followed when it changes): oil strokes, or round dabs with `pointillist()`. No need to call it again after a brush change. "Flying" = every launched piece: landed pieces stay strokes (`stats.flying` counts them all). Use a positive `lookAhead` when the clock plays backwards. `keep` (0–1) draws only that share of flying pieces, fixed per piece; lower it for large strokes (live: `mesh.material.uniforms.uKeep.value`). `removeStrokes()` switches back.
- `setDisplace({ glsl, uniforms } | null)`: GPU offset on top of the bake (see below).
- `dispose()`.
- `boom.stats`: `{ pieces, flying, secondary }`. `boom.uniforms`: shader uniforms, including the displace hook's.

Main options: pieceSize 0.25, gravity 9.81, speed [7, 18], stagger 1, spin 9, restitution 0.35, friction 0.6, stopSpeed 0.6, ground 0 (or null), solid null, snap 0, killY -50 (pieces below it stop being simulated), duration 20, step 1/90, secondary 0 (share of pieces that burst again into 8 fragments), timeWarp null, sizeScale 1, seed 4242, castShadow true, receiveShadow true, displace null, material (a MeshStandardMaterial; BakedDebris patches a clone).

Per-piece optional fields: `velocity`, `launchTime`, `burst`, `spin`, `axis`, `lifetime`.

Displace hook (GLSL, fixed signature; returns an offset in world units):

```js
displace: {
  uniforms: { uSwirl: { value: 1.5 } },
  glsl: `
    uniform float uSwirl;
    vec3 debrisDisplace(vec3 p, DebrisInfo d) {
      if (d.local <= 0.0) return vec3(0.0);   // not launched yet
      float a = uSwirl * d.local;
      return vec3(sin(a + float(d.index)), 0.0, cos(a)) * 0.3;
    }`,
}
```

`DebrisInfo`: `time` (use it, not uTime), `local` (time since launch, <= 0 = not launched), `kind` (0 piece, 1 fragment), `burst` (-1 = none), `index` (stable per piece), `rest` (local time from which the piece rests).

Oil brush look for your own effects: `import { strokeFragment } from 'baked-debris'`. For another brush: `import { strokeShaders } from 'baked-debris/shaders'; strokeShaders(brush.flying).fragment` (lower-level; your vertex shader must write `flat varying float vPiece` and `varying float vTrail` (length / width of the quad) for the pointillist look; see the fire in examples/voxel-paris).

## Pitfalls

- PainterlyPass renders the scene itself: do not add a `RenderPass` before it. It tone-maps and writes the output colour space itself: do not add an `OutputPass` after it when it is the last pass. If the scene is already display-referred, set `toneMapping: false`.
- PainterlyPass needs a `WebGLRenderer` without `logarithmicDepthBuffer` or `reverseDepthBuffer`. WebGPURenderer is not supported. It throws an error for these.
- Do not move, rotate or scale `boom.mesh` or its parents. Bakes are in world space. To place an explosion, move the pieces, bursts and `solid` before the bake.
- Changing physics options needs `rebake()`. Time, time warp and size do not.
- The displace hook does not change collisions. Large offsets push pieces through walls and the floor. Fade offsets out as `d.local` approaches `d.rest`.
- Pieces do not collide with each other. At most 6 path segments per piece.
- `material` must be a lit material such as `MeshStandardMaterial`. `MeshBasicMaterial` does not compile with the patch. For unlit pieces, use a black `MeshStandardMaterial` and add `vColor.rgb` to `totalEmissiveRadiance` in `onBeforeCompile`.
- Pieces that have not launched yet are drawn as cubes at their start position. To hide them, move them away in the displace hook while `d.local <= -0.05`; keep them in place for the last 0.05 s, so strokes point the right way at launch.
- Serve examples over HTTP (`python3 -m http.server` at the repository root); `file://` does not load ES modules.
